cells.tense: What you carried across years is standing now, finished, and you're at the table with your hands on it.
cells.ask: offer the next thing you'd pass on before it feels fully ready, and let them show you what it becomes
cells.core:
You built something meant to outlast the season you built it in, and it's standing — not perfect, but complete, and people can put weight on it. That's not luck. Somewhere along the way you chose, again and again, from what you could see clearly instead of from what was pressing on you. What got passed down here got passed down on purpose.

What you've finished is the floor other people stand on now. There's more in you that could be handed over, and the only way to find its shape is to put a piece of it in someone's hands while it's still soft. Let them work it and hand it back changed.
cells.sheetLine: You built something that will hold after you, and you're still at the table.
cells.verb: bringing a long-built thing to stand finished
cells.place: in what gets handed down between people

cells.tense: You're already standing past the finished thing, fighting to get the next one closed before it's even been opened.
cells.ask: let one person show you what the work already is to them, and change nothing until you've heard it
cells.core:
People around you are picking up what you've made and saying what it means to them, and it's already reaching further than the wheels you keep turning to push it. The pushing was useful once. It isn't doing anything for the thing now.

The version of this that holds is slower: you stand at the table, the work stands, and you let what other people carry from it come back and tell you something. Receive one piece of that before you decide one more thing. What comes back can change how you build the rest, and nothing you can add from here does.

cells.tense: You're standing back from the table where what you made gets handed on, and it's been standing there without you a while.
cells.ask: let yourself be seen knowing one thing well, without holding anything back from it
cells.core:
What you've built is still out there and still being passed around — that part hasn't stopped. You've stopped being the one who hands it over. Something in you decided the finished thing spoke for itself and stepped out of the room, and nobody has been there at the table since.

Picking up the old project and pushing at it again won't bring you back. Look at one small piece of what you know, see it clearly for exactly what it is, and let it be seen. When you stand in what you actually know instead of beside it, the room has someone in it again.

cells.tense: Your work is shaping what people carry without you in the picture, and you'd say it just turned out that way.
cells.ask: put your name on one thing you shaped and let it be yours out loud
cells.core:
There's a way of doing things where you are that other people learned from you — how a thing gets made, what counts as finished, what's worth keeping. You'd say it's just how things are done here. It isn't. Somebody chose, and the choosing has your fingerprints on it. A table like this runs on those choices, whether or not anyone calls them by your name.

Start smaller than the accomplishment you're measuring against. Standing at the table, saying clearly that this thing is yours, from a choice you actually made — that's the same act that built everything here, in its first form. Claim it and the rest follows.
